arguments.summary: Credential compromise of high-privilege service account 'svc_backup_admin' via brute-force attack originating from internal host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42). Attack involved initial Cobalt Strike beaconing, lateral movement via SMB, and privilege escalation attempts. Compromised host exhibited anomalous login behavior, unusual geolocation, and rapid access to multiple systems. Immediate containment actions included revocation of service account sessions/API keys and blocking of source IP 10.0.5.14 at the firewall.

timeline.description: Initial outbound connection from WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) to external C2 server 198.51.100.23 over HTTPS.
Suspicious process creation (rundll32 from Temp) observed on WS-FIN-042.
IDS alert triggered: 'ET TROJAN Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 Activity' from 10.0.5.42 to 198.51.100.23.
Failed Kerberos authentication attempts begin from WS-FIN-042 targeting internal systems.
Lateral movement confirmed via SMB access from WS-FIN-042 to file server 10.0.5.50.
Alert generated: Successful Kerberos authentication to domain controller using compromised service account 'svc_backup_admin'.
UEBA system flags critical risk due to anomalous login time, geolocation (Bucharest), and lateral movement pattern.
IAM/PAM system revokes all active sessions and API keys for 'svc_backup_admin'.
Firewall blocks inbound traffic from source IP 10.0.5.14 (associated with compromised host).
EPP/AV performs full scan on WS-FIN-042; detects Linux-based dropper in cron directory.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious Service Account Kerberos Brute-Force Followed by Success
logsource:
  category: authentication
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4625
    AccountName: 'svc_*'
    LogonType: 3
  filter_non_service:
    AccountName: '*admin*'
  successful_login_after_failure:
    EventID: 4624
    AccountName: 'svc_*'
    LogonType: 3
    # Correlate within 5 minutes of last failed attempt
  condition: selection | count() by AccountName, src_ip > 40 and successful_login_after_failure
level: critical
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/003/
description: Detects brute-force attacks against service accounts followed by successful authentication, indicative of credential stuffing.

arguments.summary: Credential compromise of high-privilege service account svc_backup_admin via credential stuffing attack originating from compromised host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42). Attack involved initial phishing-induced PowerShell execution, Cobalt Strike beaconing, lateral movement via SMB, and unauthorized Kerberos authentication. UEBA flagged anomalous behavior including off-hours access, geolocation deviation, and privilege escalation. IAM actions successfully revoked account sessions and API keys.

  path: /var/www/html/

  filter:

  condition: filename AND file_path AND not filter
level: critical

rule Suspicious_Chrome_Process_With_Network {
    meta:
        description = "Detects chrome.exe making network connections while spawning non-browser child processes"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "INC-AP10-V2"
        maltype = "Trojan.GenericKD"
    strings:
        $svchost_inject = "svchost.exe" wide ascii
        $c2_domain = "dynamic-c2[.]xyz" wide ascii
        $mutex = "Global\\{12345-abcde}" wide ascii
    condition:
        any of ($$) and
        process.name == "chrome.exe" and
        #network_connection and
        (process.parent.name == "explorer.exe" or process.parent.name == "userinit.exe")
}

arguments.summary: Malware infection detected on endpoint 10.0.3.15 (WS-IT-101) involving process injection of svchost.exe by Trojan.GenericKD.48571234. C2 communication initiated to internal IP 10.0.6.88, which was previously involved in network scanning activity. A webshell (.shell.php) was discovered during EPP scan. The user CORP\auser was compromised, leading to session and API key revocation. Both source and destination IPs were associated with prior scanning behavior, suggesting reconnaissance phase. Immediate containment actions included firewall block of 10.0.6.88, full isolation of 10.0.3.15 via automation, and credential revocation.

timeline.description: Network scan from 10.0.6.88 and 10.0.3.15 detected and blocked by IDS.
Normal authentication from 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101) as user CORP\helpdesk.
Malware alert triggered: Trojan.GenericKD.48571234 detected via EPP behavioral analysis on 10.0.3.15 with C2 to 10.0.6.88.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 10.0.6.88.
User CORP\auser sessions and API keys revoked via IAM/PAM system.
Endpoint 10.0.3.15 fully isolated using Ansible emergency playbook.
Full EPP scan confirms presence of Webshell.PHP.Generic.A in /var/www/html/.shell.php.

arguments.summary: Lateral movement detected from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.14) to WS-IT-101 (10.0.9.12) via PsExec service installation (PSEXESVC). Initial access achieved through phishing-driven execution of a malicious Outlook macro, leading to Cobalt Strike beacon deployment. PowerShell was used to decode and execute a payload from the Temp directory. The compromised user 'jsmith@corp.local' had elevated privileges, enabling lateral movement. Immediate containment actions included session revocation, firewall blocking of the source IP, and automated remediation of the target host using Ansible. No malware was detected during post-remediation EPP scan, and sandbox analysis of the extracted payload returned 'clean' with low confidence due to obfuscation.

Ansible playbook 'remediate_psexec.yml' executed on 10.0.9.12 to remove PSEXESVC and reset service permissions.
Full EPP scan completes on 10.0.5.14 with no threats found.

rule Suspicious_Outlook_PowerShell_Chain {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Outlook spawning PowerShell with hidden window and encoded command"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1566.001, T1059.001"
        date = "2026-04-09"
    strings:
        $powershell_exe = "powershell.exe" nocase
        $hidden_window = "-w hidden" nocase
        $encoded_command = "-encodedcommand" nocase
        $outlook_parent = "outlook.exe" nocase
    condition:
        $outlook_parent and $powershell_exe and $hidden_window and $encoded_command
}

arguments.summary: Ransomware execution was detected on host WS-IT-101 (10.0.6.30), leading to active file encryption. The host was identified as having previously conducted suspicious network scanning and was confirmed to be infected with CobaltStrike Beacon via sandbox analysis. Immediate containment actions included network isolation via firewall rules, execution of an Ansible playbook for host isolation, and password/MFA reset for the associated user. The threat actor leveraged compromised credentials and C2 infrastructure for persistence and command execution.

title: Suspicious Network Scan Followed by Beacon C2
id: 8a9b1c2d-3e4f-5a6b-7c8d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
description: Detects a sequence of events where a host performs a network scan and later establishes communication with a known or suspicious C2 server.
status: experimental
author: SOC Team
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1046/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
logsource:
    category: firewall
    product: firewall
    category: proxy
    product: proxy
detection:
    scan_event:
        event_type: network_scan
        outcome: blocked
        timeframe: 5m
    c2_event:
        dest_ip: '198.51.100.23'
        protocol: https
        bytes_out > 1000
        timeframe: 24h
    condition: scan_event and c2_event
level: high

arguments.summary: Ransomware execution was detected on host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). The incident originated from a malicious file that led to Cobalt Strike beacon deployment. The host exhibited ransomware behavior including file encryption and ransom note deployment. Immediate containment actions included network isolation of the infected host and revocation of associated user sessions and credentials. No lateral movement was confirmed, but C2 communication was established with external IPs. The host is used by the IT department and had not been involved in prior high-severity events.

arguments.summary: Ransomware execution was detected on host 10.0.6.30 (WS-IT-101), identified as a compromised IT workstation. Immediate containment actions included blocking the host at the firewall and resetting credentials for the associated user (CORP\helpdesk). No lateral movement beyond initial host confirmed.

arguments.summary: Privilege escalation incident on host WS-IT-101 (10.0.1.25) via PrintNightmare exploit (CVE-2021-34527). Attacker leveraged compromised credentials from host 10.0.5.42 (WS-FIN-042) to execute malicious DLL through spoolsv.exe. Source IP 10.0.5.14 was blocked, user CORP\auser's sessions and API keys were revoked, and host configuration hardened. No malware detected post-remediation.

Initial access and C2 beaconing from WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) to external IP 198.51.100.23.

Privilege escalation on WS-IT-101 via PrintNightmare exploit. Malicious DLL loaded from C:\Windows\Temp\malicious.dll by spoolsv.exe.
Incident response initiated. User CORP\auser sessions and API keys revoked.
Source IP 10.0.5.14 blocked via firewall rule FW-RULE-0053.
Host 10.0.1.25 reconfigured to mitigate PrintNightmare vulnerability via GPO push.
Full EPP scan completed on 10.0.1.25. No threats detected.

arguments.summary: A privilege escalation incident was detected on host 10.0.1.25 (WS-IT-101), where a local user exploited the PrintNightmare vulnerability (CVE-2021-34527) to escalate to Domain Admin. A suspicious DLL was loaded by spoolsv.exe from C:\Windows\Temp\malicious.dll. The source of the attack was traced to IP 10.0.5.14. Response actions included blocking the source IP at the firewall and revoking sessions and API keys for the affected user CORP\auser. No malware was detected during EPP scan, and initial sandbox analysis of related artifacts returned clean. Further investigation revealed no lateral movement from the host, but prior network scans and suspicious rundll32 execution were observed from another host (WS-FIN-042), indicating potential broader campaign activity.

arguments.summary: Privilege escalation incident on host WS-IT-101 (10.0.1.25) via PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-34527). Exploitation originated from compromised host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.14), linked to user CORP\jsmith. Attacker used Cobalt Strike beaconing and lateral movement via SMB. Suspicious DLL loaded by spoolsv.exe from C:\Windows\Temp\malicious.dll. Domain service account 'svc_print_mgmt' was exploited. Immediate containment actions included blocking source IP and revoking service account credentials.
